solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Boastful books linked to southern racists? (6)

blocks.note: big = boastful, as in big talk
OT = Old Testament, the usual crossword books

annotation.surface: A bragging reading list that turns out to belong to Southern racists.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that racists are only one kind of bigot, a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Racists are bigots, prejudiced against people of another race.

entries.clue: English residence turned over in broken European capital (8)

indicators.note: flipping EPAD end to end gives DAPE
the reversed piece sits inside the other
BUST means broken, the outer piece

blocks.note: bust = broken; it wraps round the rest
a pad is informal for a home

annotation.surface: An English home turned upside down somewhere in a battered European city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broken' sits at the end looking like part of the picture of a battered capital, but it supplies the outer letters, and the city itself is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain definition by category: Budapest is Hungary's capital, so one of Europe's capitals.

entries.clue: Gutted guy with back in sharp excessive pain (3)

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the ends G and Y
the back of SHARP is its final letter

annotation.surface: A disembowelled man with a sharp pain in his back.
annotation.walkthrough: GYP is British slang, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp': pain or trouble.
annotation.definitionFit: Gyp is informal British for severe pain or discomfort.

entries.clue: Cloying sentimentality born of Electra complex (7)

indicators.note: complex means intricately put together, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A psychologist's remark that mawkishness springs from the Electra complex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Electra complex' reads as one Freudian term; split it, and complex becomes the instruction to rearrange ELECTRA.
annotation.definitionFit: Treacle is used figuratively for sickly, overdone sentiment.

entries.clue: Bewilders secure dogs when cutting leads (8)

indicators.note: leads are first letters, and both words lose theirs

blocks.note: FAST = secure, minus its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone baffled by the business of tying up dogs while unclipping their leads.
annotation.walkthrough: Leads look like dog leashes; here they are the leading letters of FAST and HOUNDS.
annotation.definitionFit: To astound is to amaze or bewilder.

entries.clue: Potter’s creation country gent left oddball relatives around middle of March (8,6)

indicators.note: the whole string goes round the letter from March
the centre letter of MARCH

blocks.note: a squire is a country landowner
centre letter of MARCH, placed inside SQUIRE

annotation.surface: A country squire walking out on his eccentric family in mid-March.
annotation.walkthrough: Potter is Beatrix Potter, the English children's author, not a craftsman at a wheel. The R from March lands inside the first word, splitting the squire.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the red squirrel of The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin is one of the animal characters Beatrix Potter wrote and drew.

entries.clue: Remaining FBI agent is stuffed (7)

blocks.note: a fed is a US federal agent

annotation.surface: The last FBI agent still around has eaten far too much.
annotation.walkthrough: FED is American slang for a federal agent.
annotation.definitionFit: Stuffed means having eaten too much, overfed.

entries.clue: Continually had dingy tan refreshed (5,3,3)

indicators.note: made new again, so the letters take a new form

annotation.surface: Someone who kept topping up a dull, faded suntan.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's tan points at the beach, and 'Continually' at the start reads like an adverb for 'had'; it stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: working night and day means working around the clock, without a break.

entries.clue: Delicate caption omits euphemism for sex (6)

indicators.note: leaves out the letters IT

blocks.note: a subtitle is a caption on screen
IT, as in 'doing it', is removed

annotation.surface: A tactful caption that leaves out the coy word for sex.
annotation.walkthrough: IT for sex is an old coy usage, as in the 'It girl'; crosswords use it often.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a subtle flavour or hint is a delicate one, faint and hard to pin down.

entries.clue: Chat project on article — an easy task (5,3,6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above

blocks.note: to shoot = to project, fire forward

annotation.surface: Someone saying that chatting about the project over an article is no trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: Project reads as a noun, a piece of work; it is the verb, to fire or send out.
annotation.definitionFit: An American idiom for idle, aimless conversation, so a match for chat as a verb.

entries.clue: US semidetached de luxe shop animatedly welcomes you (6,5)

indicators.note: in a lively, jumbled way, so the letters are rearranged
takes in the U before the letters are mixed

blocks.note: U sounds like you, text-speak style

annotation.surface: An upmarket shop whose staff greet you with great enthusiasm.
annotation.walkthrough: A duplex house is American usage for a pair of homes sharing a wall, what the British call semi-detached.
annotation.definitionFit: In the US, a duplex house is a building split into two dwellings side by side.

entries.clue: Gilbert holds one metal wedge (3)

indicators.note: to hold is to have something within your grasp, so GB grips the I between its letters

blocks.note: Gb is the symbol for the gilbert, an old unit of magnetomotive force

annotation.surface: A man called Gilbert holding a metal wedge.
annotation.walkthrough: Gilbert looks like a man's name; it is the physics unit, symbol Gb.
annotation.definitionFit: A gib is a metal wedge or plate used to hold machine parts in place.

entries.clue: In favour of wrapping up address after intro is repeatedly lost in audio-recording fault (3-4)

indicators.note: PRO goes round the other piece
the first letter is dropped, then the new first letter is dropped too

blocks.clueFragment: address after intro is repeatedly lost

annotation.surface: An engineer backing a speech whose opening keeps dropping out of a recording.
annotation.walkthrough: Address is a speech, not a location; losing the intro twice strips both S and P.
annotation.definitionFit: Pre-echo is a fault where a faint copy of a sound is heard just before it, on tape or vinyl.

entries.clue: Almost entangle Republican in exploit augmented with false detail (11)

indicators.note: the last letter of EMBROIL is dropped
in means within, so the Republican is placed inside the word for exploit

blocks.note: a deed is an exploit, a feat

annotation.surface: A plot to drag a Republican into a scandal, padded out with invented details.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Almost' clips only the first word; exploit is the noun, a feat, not the verb to take advantage.
annotation.definitionFit: An embroidered story has been embellished with made-up details.

entries.clue: That which disproves half of forthcoming genuine cases (7)

indicators.note: only the first half of FUTURE is used
to case something is to put it in a case, so REAL surrounds the half-word

annotation.surface: An argument that knocks down half the genuine cases coming up.
annotation.walkthrough: Cases looks like a noun, legal cases; it is the verb, to encase.
annotation.definitionFit: A refutal is a refutation, something that proves a claim false.

entries.clue: Title bestowed upon those in the same class? (7,7)

definitions.text: Title bestowed upon those in the same class?

blocks.note: the surface reads an honour; the setter means a heading written at the top
the surface reads social class or schoolmates; the setter means items classed under one subject

annotation.surface: A grand title handed out to people of equal social rank.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads title as a rank and class as social standing; in fact the title is a heading, and the class is a category of subjects in a catalogue.
annotation.definitionFit: A subject heading is the label given to items grouped under the same topic.

entries.clue: Official instrument (8)

blocks.note: a keeper of records, or in England a part-time judge

annotation.walkthrough: In England a Recorder is a part-time judge, as well as the keeper of records; the recorder is also the wind instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: A recorder is both an official who keeps records or sits as a judge and a woodwind instrument.

entries.clue: Maybe she gave him one unneeded belt, or buckles (6,8)

indicators.note: gives way and bends out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A woman who gave a man a belt he didn't need, or a buckle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'She gave him one' is itself a double entendre: a gift, or something ruder. The definition is an example, hence 'Maybe'.
annotation.definitionFit: A double entendre is a phrase with an innocent and a risqué meaning, like 'she gave him one'.

entries.clue: Hostelry plan 50 per cent accessible to all (7)

indicators.note: only half of PUBLIC is used

blocks.note: to brew = to plan or plot, as in brewing trouble
PUBLIC = accessible to all, first half

annotation.surface: A plan for an inn that half the public can get into.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hostelry plan' reads as one phrase, a blueprint for an inn; the definition is Hostelry alone, and plan is the verb sense of brew.
annotation.definitionFit: A brewpub is a pub that brews its own beer, a kind of hostelry.

entries.clue: Cover-up that briefly leaves huge numbers in the dark (7)

definitions.text: Cover-up that briefly leaves huge numbers in the dark

blocks.note: the surface reads a scandal being hushed up; the setter means the moon covering the sun

blocks.clueFragment: that briefly leaves huge numbers in the dark
blocks.note: the surface reads the public kept uninformed; the setter means millions literally in darkness for a few minutes

annotation.surface: A scandal hushed up that keeps the public ignorant for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: Cover-up and 'in the dark' suggest political secrecy; the cover-up is the moon over the sun, and millions are briefly literally in darkness.
annotation.definitionFit: A solar eclipse covers the sun and darkens a wide area for a few minutes.

entries.clue: Country course that is set up under British (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reversed
in a down clue, these pieces come below B

annotation.surface: A nation whose course was set up under British rule.
annotation.walkthrough: Brunei was indeed a British protectorate, so the surface is historically apt.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain definition by category: Brunei, the small sultanate on Borneo, is an independent country.

entries.clue: Animal seemingly more angry having consumed drug (3,4)

indicators.note: what is consumed ends up inside the eater, so the drug goes inside the word for angrier

blocks.note: an angry face goes red, so redder looks angrier

annotation.surface: A creature that gets visibly angrier after swallowing a drug.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seemingly' is what makes REDDER fair: the colour of anger, not the thing itself.
annotation.definitionFit: The red deer is a large deer native to Britain.

entries.clue: Fox sighted incredible British cyclist cycling (5-2)

indicators.note: the last letter of HOY moves round to the front

blocks.note: a tall story is an incredible one
Sir Chris Hoy, Scottish Olympic track cyclist; cycled to YHO

annotation.surface: A British cyclist out riding spots an amazing fox.
annotation.walkthrough: Cycling is both the surface's sport and the instruction to rotate HOY to YHO.
annotation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the huntsman's cry on sighting the fox.

entries.clue: And not what Captain Horatio Hornblower ultimately offers (3)

indicators.note: take the last letter of each word

blocks.note: last letters of CaptaiN, HoratiO, HornbloweR

annotation.surface: A question about what C. S. Forester's naval hero Captain Hornblower has to offer.
annotation.walkthrough: The famous full name is there only for its endings; 'what' and 'offers' just join it to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Nor means and not, as in 'neither this nor that'.

entries.clue: Already liable Public Relations asked after withdrawn team (11)

indicators.note: drawn back, so SIDE is reversed
POSED comes after the team

annotation.surface: A PR department already on the hook, questioning a team that pulled out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Already liable' reads as legal liability; here liable means inclined or prone, which is what predisposed says.
annotation.definitionFit: Predisposed means already liable or inclined to something.

entries.clue: Jackass periodically brought up Jamaican music (3)

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so letters are taken at regular gaps
in a down clue, up means reversed

annotation.surface: A fool who was raised on Jamaican music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' reads as raised in childhood; in a down entry it tells you to write the letters upward.
annotation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican style of popular music, forerunner of reggae.

entries.clue: Biden agitated by Cruz for one owing money (8)

indicators.note: stirred up, so BIDEN's letters are rearranged
TED is placed next to the anagram

blocks.note: Ted Cruz, US senator; one Ted among many

annotation.surface: President Biden rattled by Senator Cruz.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cruz for one' points to a man named TED: Cruz is one example of a Ted.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be in debt is to owe money, and indebted is the adjective for it.

entries.clue: Fix match yet again? (6)

blocks.note: a prefix meaning again, plus a word for a matched couple, used as a verb

annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up second sense, splitting the word as RE-PAIR.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: to repair is to mend something broken, and read as re-pair it is to match things up again.
